This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased S. Mahaboob Basha, who met with road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of the petitioners case is as under:
That on 30-09-2024 at about 11-30 a.m. S. Mahaboob Basha, was riding TVS XL bearing Reg.No.AP- 03/1096 on A.Kothakota - Punganur road, Punganur Mandal,
Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh and when he reached near X-road junction, J. New town, Punganur, at that time the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TS- 3366 came in a rash and negligent manner from Palamaner side towards Madanapalle and dashed to the motorcycle of Mahaboob Basha and caused the accident.
Immediately Mahaboob Basha was shifted to Govt., Hospital, Punganur, but during the course of treatment, he succumbed to the injuries.
So far, the petitioners have spent huge amount towards funeral and obsequies ceremony.
2(a). Prior to the accident, S. Mahaboob Basha, was hale and healthy.
He was Plumber by profession in Bengaluru and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.

Due to the sudden death of S. Mahaboob Basha, petitioners have suffered mental agony Arshiya S vs Venkata Rama Rao on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30116744/
2 and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

sentences.text: 3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TS- 3366 has remained absent.

Hence he was placed ex- parte.
4.

The respondent no.2 /the Insurer of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TS-3366 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the offending lorry was not at all involved in the accident, the said lorry was falsely implicated by the petitioners in collusion with the owner and the police official to get compensation from the respondent no.2 and that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself, who suddenly came to the middle of the road in high speed and couldn't control over the vehicle and dashed to the Insured vehicle and that the deceased was not holding driving license to ride the motorcycle and not wearing helmet and that even the driver of the offending lorry was also not having valid and effective driving licence.
5.

On the basis of the above pleadings, this tribunal framed the following :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased S. Mahaboob Basha succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 30-09-2024 at about 11-30 near J.New town, Punganur Mandal, Chittoor District, Andra Pradesh due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TS- 3366?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner No.1 got examined herself as Pw1 and got examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.
The Respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

7. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative,
 Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No. 3 - As per final Order,

3  for the following:-
 REASONS  9. Issue No.1: Petitioners have categorically contended that on 30-09-2024 at about 11-30 a.m. S. Mahaboob Basha (hereinafter called deceased), was riding TVS XL bearing Reg.No.AP-03/1096 on A.Kothakota - Punganur road,
Punganur Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh and when he reached near X-road junction, J.
New town, Punganur, at that time the Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TS-3366 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner from Palamaner side towards Madanapalle and dashed to the motorcycle of Mahaboob Basha, result of which the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died in the hospital during the course of treatment.
10.

In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the wife of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 7 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P3 and Ex.P5 to 7 i.e., F.I.R with complaint, Translated copy of complaint, Inquest mahazar, Translated copy of inquest mahazar, PM report, Sketch, IMV report and Charge sheet of which are the material documents to prove the present issue.
11.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the petitioner no.1, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.394/2024 of Punganur Police Station for the offence punishable under section 106(1) of BNS.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 106(1) of BNS.
12.
The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners.
They have disputed the presence of PW.2 at the spot of accident so as to say that, PW.2 is the eye witness to the accident.
The respondent no.2 further seriously disputed the deceased working at Bangalore and eking his livelihood at Bangalore.

It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle by the deceased as the accident in question has occurred in the junction and the deceased who came from cross road suddenly entered the main road without observing the vehicle coming in the main road and hit against the offending vehicle which was proceeding in the straight road without anticipating the vehicle of the deceased.
Hence according to the learned counsel for respondent no.2 both deceased and the driver of the offending vehicle have equally contributed negligency.

So far as the presence of PW.2 is concerned it is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that, it is nowhere stated in the police records about the statement given by the PW.2 and there is no evidence that PW.2 was present at the spot of accident and that, since PW.2 is the resident of the village from which the deceased is hailed from, in order to help the petitioners, he has been implanted as the eye witness.

13. In the light of the contention taken by the respondent no.2, if the police records are perused, it is not in dispute that at the time of accident deceased was proceeding from A.Kothakota towards Punganur and offending vehicle was proceeding from Palamaneru towards Madanapalli.

sentences.text: respondent no.2 has not disputed the scene of occurrence one marked in the rough sketch at Ex.P5.
It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that the spot of accident is in the middle of the junction.
But, if the admitted document at Ex.P5 is perused the spot of accident is not in the middle of the junction but, it is on the left side of the road leads from A Kottakota towards Punganur.
It cannot be said that, the deceased was proceeding from cross road and that offending vehicle was proceeding in the main road.
Both roads are the main roads.
The deceased was proceeding in the main road leads to Punganur from A.Kottakota and offending vehicle was proceeding in the main road leads to Madanapalli from Punganur.
When both vehicles are proceeding in the straight road, when it reaches the junction, the driver of both the vehicles have to be very careful.

If the sketch is perused, the driver of the offending vehicle instead of driving his vehicle on the left side of the road took his vehicle on the extreme right side of the road and hit to the vehicle of the deceased which was proceeding on the extreme left side of A.Kottakota to Punganur.
Hence, the spot of accident clearly reveals that, it is due to the driver of the offending vehicle who drive the vehicle on the extreme right side of the road this accident has occurred.
Had the driver of the offending vehicle driven his vehicle on the left side of the road there was no even remote possibility of causing the accident.
Hence, it can be said without any hesitation that the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
14. In support of the case of the petitioners, they have examined the eye witness as PW.2.
The PW.2 has given evidence in consonance with the case of the petitioners and stated the manner in which the accident in question has occurred.
As observed supra the learned counsel for respondent no.2 has disputed the presence of the PW.2 at the spot of accident.

15. If the complaint is perused wherein the Pw.1 being the complainant has clearly stated that they have been informed about the accident by the PW.2 and that it is the PW.2 who had shifted the injured to the hospital.
Even in the charge sheet there is clear mention about the information given to the complainant about the accident by the PW.2 and shifted the injured to the hospital.
If the charge sheet witness is perused, wherein PW.2 is cited as Cw.6.
Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve the fact that PW.2 is the eye witness to the accident.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:

It is the contention taken by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 being the wife,
petitioner no.2 and 3 being the children and petitioner no. 4 and 5 being the parents of the deceased are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and that deceased was doing plumber work and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
17.
It is stated by the petitioners that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 27 years.
The petitioners have produced Aadhar card of the deceased which reflects the date of birth of deceased as 01-01-1997 as per Ex.P4.
Hence as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 27 years.

18. So far as the deceased working as Plumber at Bangalore is concerned, the learned counsel for respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the said fact and submitted that the deceased was working at Arshiya S vs Venkata Rama Rao on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30116744/
5 his home town and that in order to file petition before the Bangalore court so as to get higher compensation, the petitioners have wrongly stated in the petition that, the deceased was working at Bangalore.

sentences.text:
It is further argued by the learned counsel that if the petition is filed at Andrapradesh Court, the petitioners will get lesser compensation because at Andrapradesh court, the notional income will be taken only Rs.9,000/- p.m. but in Karnataka the notional income will be considered at higher rate, hence, submitted to consider the notional income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- p.m.
19.

In the light of the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 if the materials placed on record is perused, it is true that in the complaint it is no where stated that deceased was working at Bangalore, but in the petition they have stated that deceased was working at Bangalore.

It is true that the petitioners are the resident of Chittoor District, Andra Pradesh, the respondent No.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle is also from Vijayawada, Andrapradesh State, the accident in question has occurred at Punganur Mandal, Chittoor District, Andrapradesh State.
But, the respondent no.2 i.e., the insurer of the offending vehicle had the office at Bangalore,
hence, it can be said that, this court has jurisdiction to try the petition.
Hence, when petition is filed before this court, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased which this court usually considers in all the other cases.
20. As observed earlier, it is contended by the petitioners that deceased was doing Plumber work and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2024, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.

Hence, taking into consideration the age and year of accident,
this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
21.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 being the minor children and petitioner No.4 and 5 are parents of the deceased, they are the dependents of the deceased.

22. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, minor children and parents,
1/4th of the annual income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses and remaining 3/4th is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

23. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case, as deceased was aged around 27 years, 40% should be added towards future prospects.

Arshiya S vs Venkata Rama Rao on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30116744/
6 24.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/-, by adding 40% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.23,100/-, out of it if 1/4th is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.17,325/-
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 26 to 30 is '17'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.35,34,300/-
(Rs.17,325/- x 17 x 12 =35,34,300/-).
25. Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost her husband and petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father and petitioner no.4 and 5 have lost their son.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

26. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
27.

In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
 UNDER THE HEADS AMOUNT  1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150-00  2 Transportation and funeral Rs. 18,150-00  expenses  3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs. 2,42,000-00  parental consortium and  filial consortium  (Rs.48,400x5)
4 Loss
of dependency

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.38,12,600/- Rupees Thirty Eight Lakh Twelve Thousand Six Hundred Only) and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the findings on issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.3 :- In the light of findings given on Issue No. 1 and 2, my finding on this point is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.38,12,600/- (Rupees Thirty Eight Lakh Twelve Thousand Six Hundred Only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the amount with interest within 2 months from the date of award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.20,12,600/- Petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.5,00,000/- each Petitioner No.4 & 5 are entitled for Rs.4,00,000/- each

Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1, 4 & 5 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification.

The entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of minor petitioner no.2 and 3 till they attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioners to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minor.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 3rd day of October 2025)
